issues.problem: The skill treats every scoped block defining a pack-owned ESLint rule as conflicting, claiming the pack rules reach those files and that no placement keeps both. This is false for Expo's no-restricted-syntax, which only covers **/components/**/*; a user rule scoped to scripts/**/*.js or src/features/**/*.ts can coexist without overlap.
issues.suggested_fix: Check whether the app block's file scope overlaps the specific pack rule's coverage before declaring a conflict. Keep the 'no placement keeps both' warning only for overlapping files.
issues.failure_scenario: Setup finds an app-owned selector in a scripts-only block and tells the developer it must replace that selector or leave the tokens rule unmeasured, though both stay effective in their disjoint scopes.
issues.evidence: packages/cookwright/packs/expo/eslint.cjs:92 scopes the no-restricted-syntax block to '**/components/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}' only. SKILL.md:164 says any block counts "whatever its files scope (a block on src/features/**/*.ts or scripts/**/*.js counts: the pack's rules reach those files too)" and that "no placement keeps both". That is false for no-restricted-syntax: a block scoped to scripts/ or src/features/ (outside components) has no overlap with the pack's block, so both selectors stay effective. It does hold for Expo's i18next (eslint.cjs:84, '**/*.{tsx,jsx}') and max-lines-per-function (:108-109, all ts/js/tsx/jsx), and for supabase's no-restricted-imports (supabase/eslint.cjs:22, all ts/tsx/js/jsx), so the overstatement is limited to Expo's no-restricted-syntax. The effect is an unneeded conflict warning and a needless ask, so P3 is right.

issues.location: tableKeys, line 186 (the header test `SEPARATOR.test(lines[i + 1])`), with SEPARATOR at line 82
issues.problem: This round's fix covers spaced thematic breaks (`- - -`, `* * *`) but not the most common one, a bare `---`. When `---` sits directly under a table's last body row, it matches SEPARATOR, so tableKeys treats that last row as a header row and drops it. In GFM a thematic break ends the table and the row above it is a body row. The guide's new sentence about thematic breaks and the entries.mjs header both suggest breaks are handled, which is wider than the code.
issues.suggested_fix:
Treat a row as a header only when the line before it is not a table row (the table's first line) and the separator has the same number of cells as the row. Add a test: `| P |
| --- |
| Button |
| Card |
---` gives Button and Card. If that is out of scope for this round, add it to E-052 under backlog discipline.

The thematic-break handling (BREAK, line ~112, used only in items()) only stops list-marker parsing and never ends a table. A bare `---` directly under the last body row makes that row read as a header and drop its key.

issues.location: the thematic-break test added in f41d92b (`// Two markers are not a break: the nested item's content starts at column 4.`); MARKER at entries.mjs line 109
issues.problem: The new test comment describes a mechanism the code does not have. MARKER needs one or more spaces after a marker, so a marker at the end of a line (`- -`, or a bare `-` or `10.`) opens no item. `- -` opens only the outer item at column 2, and the test passes because 4 spaces is 2 columns past that. In CommonMark an empty-start item's content starts at marker width + 1, and the reader ignores this, so the guide's 'a line read from where its list item's content starts' is wider than the code for such items.
issues.suggested_fix: Let MARKER match a marker followed by end of line, with content at marker width + 1 (CommonMark 5.2, empty-start item). Add tests `-\n    ## Button` gives Button and `- -\n      ## X` gives X. Otherwise fix the comment and add the empty-start item to E-052's list of what the declared grammar does not read.
issues.failure_scenario: A contract doc with `-` on its own line, then `    ## Button` (4 spaces). CommonMark reads that as a heading inside the item (content column 2), but docKeys returns no Button (probed), so doctor names Button missing. The same happens with `10.` then `    ## Button`, and with `- -` then `      ## X` (6 spaces).
issues.evidence:
entries.mjs:109 MARKER requires ( +) after the marker, so a marker at end of line opens no item. I probed docKeys: '-
    ## Button' -> [], '10.
    ## Button' -> [], '- -
      ## X' -> [], while '-
  ## Button' -> ['Button']. CommonMark puts the content of an empty-start item at marker width + 1, so those 4-space and 6-space headings are headings inside the item, but the reader drops them as code. entries.test.mjs:237-238: '- -
    ## Nested' passes because only the outer item opens (content column 2, so 4 spaces is 2 columns past it). The comment 'Two markers ... nested item's content starts at column 4' is wrong about the mechanism.
